newsitem.title: ITALY: Bergamo to extend runway, upgrade cargo facilties.
newsitem.headline: Bergamo to extend runway, upgrade cargo facilties.

text.p: Bergamo airport is to invest 80 billion lire in upgrading facilities including 50 billion lire reserved for a cargo centre and related infrastructures, an airport authority (SABCO) spokesman said.
Work is expected to be completed by the year 2000 and will begin in the next few weeks and at least 30 percent of the new infrastructure is due to be ready for use by end-1998, he told Reuters.
Part of the investment will also be used to extend the runway to 3,160 metres from 2,860 metres, he added.
The cargo centre will be built in the northern part of the airport and will be accessed by a dedicated cargo road.
SABCO said the work includes the provision of parking space for seven medium sized planes.
Bergamo is the Italian operation hub for air express operators DHL Worldwide Express,United Parcel Service of America UPS, and TNT TNT.AX who now use Boeing 727s.

There will also be two parking spaces for wide body freighters. The airport is able to handle freighters equivalent to McDonnell Douglas DC-10s but not fully loaded Boeing 747Fs, the spokesman said. -- Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax:5017
